THE PREAMBLE, verbatim:
## Slice two units

One row is one PR, from main, signed and through the merge queue after the
operator rules. Follow this order. Dependencies are semantic prerequisites,
not simply the preceding row; the independence of U1–U4 is explicit in D9.
No row through U9a2 lifts the MCP compile fence. U9b is the sole enabling PR.
The lettered splits are required by the checked seams: record schema plus
embedded copy already consumes two files; multi-server wiring crosses runtime,
protocol and adapter data; storage/folding/inspect crosses CLI, protocol,
runtime and pure view. Minimal ledger writing is deliberately pulled into U6.

`contracts/realms.v<N>.schema.json` denotes one exact future file allocated
as **the next realms version after v7** at U5c, including v7's fields. It is
the only intentionally deferred filename number. Every other production path
below is literal. New paths are proposed modules/schemas, not files created
by this document plan. Constructors/registration are counted in their row.
Future tests extend the named suites; capability_broker already exists under
the consolidated CLI integration binary. New capability_artifacts and runtime
capability_ledger/capability_broker_launch modules are registered through the
existing test-only roots (CLI tests/it.rs and runtime tests/it.rs), not new
undeclared binaries. Tests may use child modules of the owning suites to stay
below 2,000 lines; list every test move in unit evidence.

Each row closes exactly its numbered tasks, including tests/mutations and
gate evidence. Test lists below are the allowed owning suites; every row
also updates this change's tasks and later implementation evidence. Measured
witness/compose pins accompany only rows that change their inputs.

YOUR ROW, verbatim:
| U9a1 | U8g, U2 | Move doctor's capability reporting into its module; 45.7–45.8 | `crates/brokkr-cli/src/doctor.rs`; `crates/brokkr-cli/src/doctor/capabilities.rs` |

YOUR UNIT, verbatim:
### U9a1 — Move doctor's capability reporting into its module

Move doctor's capability reporting out of `doctor.rs` into its private child `doctor/capabilities.rs`, declared from `doctor.rs`: the scope and disposition words, the native assessments, `report_capabilities` and the grant reporting it calls, with the imports only they use. Split `report_capabilities`, since a moved function meets the function-length and complexity ceilings as a new entry. Name the three states of the read map's optional binding (no binding read, a grant that failed, a native binding) with a local enum in place of `Some(&None)` and `Some(&Some(..))`, which closes U2's carried LOW. Doctor prints every line it prints today, in the same order and words, and nothing new. No public item changes.

Operator ruling 2026-10-21 splitting U9a (in chat, "A"): U9a is split in two. U9a1 moves doctor's capability reporting into `doctor/capabilities.rs` and changes nothing doctor prints. U9a2 reads each seat's whole capability plan through the planner compile uses, and reports what compile would judge, without compiling past the MCP fence: compile's refusal of every MCP grant stands until U9b. Beside its doctor files and binding.rs, U9a2 may change `crates/brokkr-runtime/src/capabilities.rs`, `crates/brokkr-runtime/src/bundle.rs`, `crates/brokkr-runtime/src/bundle/mcp.rs` and `crates/brokkr-runtime/src/agents/mcp.rs`, to reach that planner, the bundle's declared binding minimum and U1g1's strict-isolation verdict. Its public API rise is approved up to +15 lines across quality/public-api/*.txt together (operator ruling 2026-10-21, "+15 is fine"); a larger rise comes back to the operator.

Closes tasks 45.7 and 45.8; requirements [SC5](specs/slice-two-contracts/spec.md), [SD3](specs/slice-two-delivery/spec.md).
Proof: Every existing doctor capability test passes unchanged against the moved module; each of the three binding states' lines is pinned exactly; an independent removal of one state's arm fails its own test.

Owning tests: `crates/brokkr-cli/src/doctor/capability_tests.rs`.

CONTROLLER GUIDANCE (the controller's; check it against the code, it grants no scope):
- This is a move and a split with no behaviour change. Prove it: every existing test in doctor/capability_tests.rs and doctor/tests.rs passes unchanged except for the path a test calls, and `brokkr doctor`'s output for the existing fixtures is byte-identical. - Leave engine/broker.rs's `const STARTUP: Duration = Duration::from_secs(30);` exactly as it is (the peer controller's #803 test reads that line).

STANDING RULINGS. Decision 0065's hold: off by default, no grandfathering; realm-only grants; tools are an abstraction, dialects the concrete; refuse, never reconcile (slice one's operator ruling of 2026-09-23). The MCP compile fence stays in place until U9b. Hosts are Linux and macOS only (decision 0063). Main's code-health rules bind: no `unsafe` in brokkr-runtime; `#[expect(.., reason)]`, never `#[allow]`; clippy's too_many_lines, excessive_nesting and struct_excessive_bools are denied, so split, and only if splitting would widen your unit carry `reason = "baseline 2026-09-29, decision 0065 slice one merged with main; split after #319"`; when a count moves, re-measure quality/'s file-lines, too-many-lines and suppressions (the steps quality/measure.sh uses), witness pins with `BROKKR_BLESS=1 cargo test -p brokkr-runtime --test witness_digests` (or, once #423's single test binary is on your base — crates/brokkr-runtime/tests/it.rs exists — `BROKKR_BLESS=1 cargo test -p brokkr-runtime --test it witness_digests::`), and budgets with scripts/measure-budgets.sh. Where a crate has tests/it.rs, a NEW tests/*.rs file must be registered as `mod <file>;` in that crate's tests/it.rs (layering::test_targets refuses an unregistered one), unless it sets HOME, cwd, env or a global allocator, in which case it is its own [[test]] in Cargo.toml with the reason written there; and `--test <file>` filters become `--test it <file>::` (capability_launch stays its own binary).

RULES. Touch at most the production files your row names; if the real scope exceeds them, STOP and report `oversized` with the split. One exception, the operator's standing rule of 2026-10-09 (operator-ruling-2026-10-03.md): beside a production file in your row that sits at its 800-line ceiling, or is frozen at its quality/file-lines.txt baseline above it, you may add NEW private child modules, declared from that file, in its own module tree and consumed in this unit, without stopping. The same holds beside a row file that your own change would push past 800 lines (extended 2026-10-11). You may also change an EXISTING private child module of a file in your row, in that file's own module tree (extended 2026-10-11). You may move existing code out of the full file into such a child to make room, preferring the code your change touches. Name each new file in your evidence and commit, and set its quality/file-lines.txt row. You may also add a name to an EXISTING re-export in the parent module that declares one of your row's files, where the parent's line count does not change (extended 2026-10-10). Files in any other module tree still mean `oversized`; any public API growth still needs the operator's ruling at PR time (record it, do not stop). Test files are NOT bounded by the row (controller's standing clarification, 2026-10-05): a test anywhere that pins behaviour your unit changes, a validator or fixture swap in another suite, or a new child test module beside an owning suite that sits over its line ceiling is part of your unit — size-neutral wherever a file sits at its quality/file-lines.txt baseline. A LOW finding you cannot fix inside your row's production files: record it in your result and do NOT report blocked for it. Tests assert exact reasons and values, never is_err(); every new test is bound by a compiling mutation that makes it fail, then restored, recorded (test, assertion) in evidence.md. Tick a task in tasks.md only on observed evidence; record results in a NEW file of your own, openspec/changes/decision-0065-capabilities-slice-two/evidence/U9a1.md (two lanes deliver units at once, and every unit appending to evidence.md made each pair of pull requests conflict), and do not edit evidence.md itself; write it in prose or a table — never as a bullet list of the standard gate lines (`cargo fmt ...: clean`, `cargo clippy ...: clean`), which earlier evidence files already hold word for word, so the data clone gate refuses it; never edit the tasks.md preamble. Fixtures build on a canonicalised temporary root; no test reads .forge/ or needs an installed provider. Frozen contracts, policy/phase-machine.json, fixtures/, reference/ and extensions/ do not move unless your unit names them. Sign every commit (`git commit -S`; main requires signatures). HEADLESS SEAT: your session ends the moment you end a turn — never run a command in the background, never use Monitor or ScheduleWakeup, run every command in the foreground under the tool's 10-minute limit (suites crate by crate with `timeout 590`, split by --lib/--test if longer), and write your result file before you finish. GATES: cargo fmt --all -- --check; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings; the suite of each crate you touched; openspec validate --all --strict; typos --hidden; git diff --check; quality/ratchet.sh files and clones. CI also builds and tests on macOS, which this host cannot: Linux-only code (namespaces, mountinfo, /proc, device numbers, Linux-only syscalls) goes behind `#[cfg(target_os = "linux")]` with a non-Linux stand-in that refuses, as broker/session.rs does, and any libc or rustix type you use must be the same type on both (rustix's Dev is u64 on Linux and i32 on macOS; U6c6a's first PR failed to compile there). Keep the session small; commit when the unit is done; never push.

instructions.analyze:
# OpenSpec analyze

Judge duplication, ambiguity, underspecification, house alignment, coverage gaps, and inconsistency across proposal, deltas, design and tasks. Treat the realm house as the constitution. Return each finding with severity and its earliest owning artifact; zero findings is consistent.
instructions.clarify:
# OpenSpec clarify

Judge underspecified areas, unquantified language, missing decisions, capability/delta mismatches, and requirements without adequate scenarios. Return every ambiguity with the evidence needed to settle it; zero findings is clear.
instructions.design:
# OpenSpec design

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/design.md`. Record context, goals and non-goals, decisions with alternatives, risks, migration, and open questions. On return, revise the design and dependent artifacts so no finding is merely acknowledged.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.
instructions.implement:
# OpenSpec tasks

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/tasks.md` as numbered groups of checkboxes. Name the requirement served by every task. On return, repair the breakdown and its requirement coverage before implementation resumes.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.

Change location: `openspec/changes/{change}`. Archive operation: ["openspec","archive","{change}","--yes"].

# OpenSpec archive

Folding a change is the last task: run the archive operation named above,
which moves the change directory under `openspec/changes/archive/` and
folds its deltas into `openspec/specs/`. Folding also records which change
wrote which capability, so every capability the change touched carries a
`## Provenance` list.

After the archive operation, open each capability's
`openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md` that the change touched and append
exactly one line under a `## Provenance` heading held at the end of the
file:

`- \`<archived-directory-name>\` — folded <YYYY-MM-DD>`

`<archived-directory-name>` is the directory the archive operation
created under `openspec/changes/archive/`; `<YYYY-MM-DD>` is the day it
was folded. Append only: never rewrite, reorder or remove an existing
provenance line, because standing truth accumulates and is not edited into
a different meaning. The line is a pointer, not a summary — it names the
change and nothing else, and the why stays in the change directory.

This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, and `reference/` (its schemas included) are
read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `recipes/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

The supported hosts are Linux and macOS (decision 0063); WSL2 is Linux. Write
no Windows-conditional code, test or evidence.

## Architecture

Decision 0071 rules how code here is shaped. Build to it, and cite its ruling
numbers in what you judge. Where a gate named below holds a rule, the gate is
the authority, and a finding it would catch is the gate's.

- **Pure core (ruling 1).** `brokkr-core` and `brokkr-view` do no I/O and read
  no clock, environment or randomness. They run no process. Pass `now`, paths
  and environment in as arguments. Effects live in the crates above core and
  view, and are journaled.
- **Enums and data, not traits (ruling 2).** A closed set is an enum matched
  exhaustively, with no wildcard arm that decides behaviour. Anything an
  operator extends is data under `adapters/`, `agents/`, `recipes/` or
  `realms.json`, validated and digested. Add a trait only for a seam whose
  contract spans several operations that must stay consistent with one
  another, reached across a process or service boundary, and name that seam
  in its doc comment. `ProducerTransport` is the one such trait today. A test
  double alone does not make a seam: a single substitutable function is a
  closure seam (`*_with`, `*_in`), which is how the house inverts a
  dependency otherwise.
- **Typed at the edge (ruling 3).** Parse wire, file and harness data once
  into a type, with `serde` and `deny_unknown_fields` where the contract is
  closed. `serde_json::Value` never goes past the edge, into state, or back
  out by string key. Never put `format!("{:?}")` in anything digested or
  journaled. A doubly-optional field or a string vocabulary is a missing enum.
- **Small functions (ruling 4).** New and changed functions stay within 100
  lines, nesting depth 5 and 7 parameters. Cyclomatic complexity follows
  the operator's 2026-09-26 ruling: a function may reach the higher of 15
  and its baseline, so a new function stays within 15, an existing one may
  change freely up to 15, and one already over 15 may only shrink.
  Production files stay within 800 lines and test files within 2,000, and a
  file already over may not grow. Add no new `jscpd` clone in production
  code, test code or data. `quality/` holds the measured baseline. Today's
  offenders carry `#[allow(clippy::…)]`, and #337 converts them to
  `#[expect(clippy::…, reason = "…")]`. Add a suppression only by a ruling,
  and remove it when you fix the function. A new suppression is
  `#[expect(…, reason)]`, never `#[allow]`.
- **Once (ruling 5).** Every fact has one home. A repeated vocabulary, skeleton
  or helper becomes one function or one table. An agent is defined once under
  `agents/`, and seats hire it by reference. A recipe that differs from another
  by a model, a seat or an entry is an `extends` overlay, never a copy. The
  agent library does not yet accept `extends`, and #360 builds it. Until then,
  a variation of an agent lives at the seat that hires it, overridden in a
  recipe overlay. It is never a second agent file that restates the first. A
  copy that must exist, such as a script a bundle pins, is held to its source
  by a test.
- **Nothing unused (ruling 6).** Add no alias, agent, contract version, flag or
  `pub` item without a consumer, and prefer `pub(crate)`. A deprecation names
  the release that removes it.
- **One derivation (ruling 7).** A fact shown on two surfaces is derived once
  in `brokkr-view`. The CLI, the TUI and `ui.html` only paint it. The engine
  never admits anything by a display-crate function.
- **Typed errors (ruling 8).** Return a `thiserror` enum whose `Display` keeps
  the operator's text. Tests match variants and pin each module's text once.
  Add no new `Result<_, String>`.
- **Tests that bind (ruling 9).** Assert exact values or variants, never
  `is_err()` alone. Show that every new test binds: a compiling mutation that
  removes the behaviour must make it fail. Restore the behaviour and record
  the failing test. Share fixtures through builders. Never change the process
  environment without a guard that restores it on unwind. A production guard
  left out because the exact-coverage gate would count it unreachable carries
  a removal-control test for the invariant that makes it unreachable, and the
  comment explaining the omission names that test.
- **The house's patterns (ruling 10).**
  - A harness is a module behind `AdapterKind`. This is the target form;
    today all five kinds share one module, and #347 and #348 build the
    split.
  - A CLI verb is a `Cmd` variant plus a handler.
  - A long parameter list becomes a parameter object.
  - Argv and mount tables are built with a builder.
  - Observing the world is split from deciding on it.
  - Never use a trait-object registry for a closed set.

Judges rate a finding against these rulings by this table, and cite the ruling
number:

- **info:** something a house gate would catch. The gate's verdict is the
  authority.
- **low:** a new or changed function over a ceiling, a rule written a second
  time, an item added without a consumer, or a `Value` carried past its edge
  within one module.
- **medium:** an untyped vocabulary that crosses crates, recipe or agent data
  copied instead of extended, a fact derived a second time on another surface,
  an error matched by its text, or a new test that cannot fail.
- **high or above:** any violation that hides a fail-open path or weakens a
  refusal. It is carried as a security finding.

A principle the implementer bent knowingly, and named with its reason in
`notes`, is still rated, and the judge carries that reason with the finding.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.

```json
{
  "repository": "feedback-loop-ai/brokkr",
  "default_branch": "main",
  "tag_format": "v{version}",
  "version_files": ["Cargo.toml", "Cargo.lock"],
  "version_update": "Bump the workspace package and six path-dependency versions together. Run cargo update --workspace --offline without upgrading registry dependencies. Measure and update the witness and compose manifest digests because the engine version participates in their identity.",
  "release_notes": "docs/releases/v{version}.md",
  "handoff_directory": "docs/releases/v{version}",
  "scratch_directory": ".forge/release",
  "documentation": ["README.md", "ARCHITECTURE.md", "CONTRIBUTING.md", "docs/guides/", "packaging/README.md"],
  "validation": [
    {"name": "format", "command": "cargo fmt --all -- --check"},
    {"name": "clippy", "command": "cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings"},
    {"name": "tests", "command": "cargo test --workspace --all-features --locked"},
    {"name": "self bundle", "command": "cargo run --locked -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle recipes/self"},
    {"name": "verify bundle", "command": "cargo run --locked -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle recipes/verify"},
    {"name": "exact coverage", "instructions": "Run bash scripts/coverage-exact.sh in CI or host validation outside the workspace box before tagging. Boundary tests require creating a namespace, which the box deliberately refuses to nest. Record this check as pending in the preparation handoff until that external result exists; never lower the coverage gate."},
    {"name": "release binary", "command": "cargo build --release --locked -p brokkr-cli"},
    {"name": "remote CI", "instructions": "Before tagging, require all applicable CI jobs on the final candidate commit, including both supported operating systems, MSRV, licenses, audit, packaging and exact coverage."}
  ],
  "organization_profiles": [
    {"repository": "feedback-loop-ai/.github", "path": "profile/README.md", "project_url": "https://github.com/feedback-loop-ai/brokkr", "apply": "after verified publication"}
  ],
  "channels": [
    {"name": "GitHub release", "evidence": "Four platform archives, Linux deb/rpm packages, SHA256SUMS and signed build provenance."},
    {"name": "crates.io", "evidence": "All seven workspace crates serve the new version."},
    {"name": "apt and rpm", "evidence": "The signed Pages repositories index the new packages."},
    {"name": "Homebrew and Nix", "evidence": "The generated channel PRs are merged and their versions and digests match the release manifest."}
  ],
  "extensions": [
    {"name": "workflow toolchain agreement", "instructions": "Check that CI, release admission and local coverage select the same pinned compiler.", "evidence": "Both workflows and coverage-exact.sh consume rust-nightly-version.txt."},
    {"name": "frozen contracts", "instructions": "Compare contracts, fixtures, policy/phase-machine.json and reference against the previous release; explain additive versions and flag modifications to frozen bytes.", "evidence": "A reviewed diff with migration notes for any new contract versions."}
  ]
}
```

result.notes: Framing: .forge/tasks/u9a1-doctor-capabilities.md. Ruled chore under the explicit 2026-10-03 operator directive and accepted U9a1 split: a private doctor extraction, bounded function split and local three-state enum, preserving output and public API (0071 rulings 2-4 and 9). Source confirms the 1562-line file, 184-line/CC37 reporting function and nested optional binding. Scope is tasks 45.7-45.8; U9a2 reporting and U9b enablement remain excluded. Full engine council review remains required by the commission. Inspected the staged split and named rules/spec/code only; preserved delivery files and staged changes. No implementation or recipe selection.

U9a1 is done in signed commit 73d2eab1 on s2/U9a1, base cb89e119. Doctor's capability block (scope_words through report_grant, plus the imports only it used) moved whole into the new private child crates/brokkr-cli/src/doctor/capabilities.rs (541 lines), declared from doctor.rs, which drops from 1562 to 1141 lines. report_capabilities is split along its phases: load_adapters, mapped_realms, report_realm, report_adapter, report_native and wanted. Every function is at cyclomatic 10 or below (cargo crap, no LCOV), and both of its #[expect]s are gone. Clippy -D warnings is clean. U2's carried LOW is closed: the read map's Option<Option<..>> is now a private enum Binding {Unread, Failed, Native{grant, provider, key}}, matched with no wildcard. report_grant keeps its Option return, so its existing test is unchanged. Only report_capabilities and report_grant are pub(super). No public item changed: doctor is a private module, and quality/public-api did not move. Output check: brokkr doctor printed byte-identical output (cmp, same sha256) before and after the change on a four-realm fixture, on a map that is not JSON and on the repository itself. Tests: existing tests keep their assertions and change only the path they call. capability_tests.rs went from 1978 to 1970 lines. Three new tests in the child doctor/capability_tests/binding_tests.rs pin each state's full report. Each failed under its own compiling mutation (Unread at :19, Failed at :40, Native at :61) and so did the provider guard (at :84); the other two tests passed each time, and all passed after restoring. Suites passed: brokkr-cli lib 1000, it 780, the other brokkr-cli targets, all other crates' targets and doctests. init_doctor 27, doc_truth 19, suppressions 6. recipes/self compiles, openspec strict passes 31/31, and fmt, typos and git diff --check (staged and unstaged) are clean. Baselines: the file-lines rows for doctor.rs, capabilities.rs, capability_tests.rs and binding_tests.rs; the report_capabilities row removed from too-many-lines and the two_off_controls row moved to :1323; suppressions production too_many_lines 21->20 and excessive_nesting 10->9; four moved doctor.rs entries removed from crap-baseline. No baseline was raised. Evidence is in openspec/changes/decision-0065-capabilities-slice-two/evidence/U9a1.md, and tasks 45.7 and 45.8 are ticked. PENDING: this seat refused to execute quality/ratchet.sh and jscpd ('requires approval'), so ratchet files, clones, crap and api are unobserved. The file sizes were checked by hand against the rule. Exact coverage and the macOS CI legs are also pending. Not pushed.

members.adversarial: Security review: clean. The moved block's message literals are preserved (the only text difference is the loop-variable spelling 'capabilities {realm}' -> 'capabilities {name}'), and the old (Some(grant), bound==Some(&None)) mapping is reproduced exactly by Binding::{Native,Failed,Unread}: Native matching provider+key = granted/ok-warn, Failed = UNKNOWN/warn, Unread and Native-of-another-provider = NOT granted/warn; report.missing/healthy classifications, safe()/Safe escapings, plan calls and line order are unchanged, so no refusal is weakened. No public item changed (only pub(super); quality/public-api untouched), and nothing touches journaling, secrets, seat/driver/protocol input or compile's MCP fence. One non-security gate residual: quality/ratchet.sh clones refuses with 2 new test-code clones because the new 'mod binding_tests;' line sits immediately above the already-baselined 'write' helper and extends its fragment (capability_tests.rs:11 vs brokkr-runtime/src/capabilities/tests.rs:7 and tests/capability_launch.rs:38); base cb89e119 passes and a simulated move of 'mod binding_tests;' to the end of capability_tests.rs makes the ratchet pass. Ruling 4/5, gate-caught, so info. quality/ratchet.sh files and baselines hold; doctor:: 95 tests and init_doctor 27 pass (the first init_doctor run failed only because the harness injects a malformed GIT_CONFIG_COUNT; rerun with it unset is green).
members.correctness: Correctness review of 73d2eab1 (U9a1). The move is faithful. I compared the old report_capabilities with the new chain (load_adapters, mapped_realms, report_realm, report_adapter, report_native, wanted) phase by phase. The warnings come out in the same order, including the Err(world) path: the warning, then report_native_assessments, then return. The message strings are byte-identical. Natives are iterated in the same BTreeMap order. The Binding enum's arms map exactly onto the old (granted, bound == Some(&None)) match. A Native with a matching (provider, key) gives the granted line. Failed gives UNKNOWN (the old (None, true)). Unread, and a Native bound elsewhere, give NOT granted (the old (None, false)). The grant carried in Native is the one grants.get(capability) returned before. The match is exhaustive with no wildcard (ruling 2). The U2 LOW is closed. No public item moved. report_capabilities and report_grant are pub(super), which the sibling test module needs. Both #[expect]s are gone, the quality rows (file-lines, too-many-lines, suppressions, crap-baseline) are updated consistently, and `quality/ratchet.sh files` holds in this seat. The three new binding_tests pin whole reports, and the recorded mutations are plausible and independent. FINDING (LOW, decision 0071 ruling 4, gate-caught): `quality/ratchet.sh clones` FAILS on this head with 2 new test-scope clones not in the baseline. One is crates/brokkr-cli/src/doctor/capability_tests.rs:11 vs brokkr-runtime/src/capabilities/tests.rs:7 (9 lines). The other is the same span vs brokkr-runtime/tests/capability_launch.rs:38 (7 lines). I ran the same check on an export of main cb89e119 and it holds there, so this commit introduced both clones. The cause is the new header lines (`use brokkr_core::realms::CapabilityGrant; use brokkr_runtime::realms::World; mod binding_tests;`) ahead of the shared `fn write` helper: the token run now matches the runtime suites' identical header+write. The implement seat could not run the ratchet and recorded clones as 'unobserved' while asserting no clone. CI's clone ratchet will go red. A minimal fix keeps the old fully-qualified paths in the two call sites, or moves the imports/mod below the helpers; a re-baseline would need a ruling. The evidence's Pending section should then record the observed verdict. INFO: Binding::Unread is never stored, only used as the default for an absent key. That is acceptable and documented. design.md repeats the operator's split-ruling paragraph in both the U9a1 and U9a2 sections. That was the controller's staged prep, and the data clone scope held. Nothing smells of security.
members.security: Security review of cb89e119..73d2eab1 (U9a1: doctor capability reporting moved to doctor/capabilities.rs and split). Compared the moved block line by line with the original. Fail-closed reading preserved: a native line reads 'granted' only when the realm's grant validated ALONE and binds exactly this (provider, key), which is now Binding::Native with a provider==provider && key==key guard, the same as the old `bound == Some(&ours)`. The grant a Native binding carries is the same `grants[capability]` the old `grants.get(capability)` returned, because `read` is keyed by that capability. A grant that failed to validate (Binding::Failed) still reads UNKNOWN, never denied or granted. A Native binding to another provider or key, like no grant at all (Unread), still reads NOT granted. So no path upgrades a failed or foreign grant to a grant. The unreadable map still returns early with only the native assessments and invents no empty grant set. report.missing still marks the report unhealthy for failed grants and unreadable definitions. Sanitising is unchanged: Safe::new and safe wrap the same adapter-derived and evidence text as before, and the bounded_line sink still carries refusal causes. Visibility: report_capabilities and report_grant became pub(super), private to the doctor module tree and used only by its tests. No public item changed. Nothing here touches the journal, seat results, driver output or protocol messages, and doctor still runs nothing. Removing the two #[expect] suppressions and their baseline rows (too-many-lines, suppressions, crap) is consistent with the split. No existing test assertion was weakened: only the call paths in capability_tests.rs changed. No findings.
members.spec-compliance: Reviewed the entire cb89e119..73d2eab1 diff against the settled U9a1 design, tasks 45.7-45.8, SC5/SD3 and decision 0071. The private extraction, phased split and exhaustive three-state Binding enum satisfy the functional scope; existing assertions remain intact, and the three new exact-output tests have recorded independent compiling removal failures. No public API, MCP compile fence, frozen files or out-of-row production files changed. Independently observed: 95 doctor tests, 27 init_doctor tests and 19 doc_truth tests pass; formatting, workspace all-target/all-feature clippy, strict OpenSpec (31 items), full typos, diff check, file-size ratchet and recipes/self compilation pass. Measured moved functions have cyclomatic complexity at most 10. Residual I1 (info; return to smith; decision 0071 rulings 4 and 5, SD2 and task 45.8): the required clone gate fails on this head. `timeout 590 bash quality/ratchet.sh clones`, using pinned jscpd 5.3.2, exits 1 with two new test clones: (a) 9 lines at crates/brokkr-cli/src/doctor/capability_tests.rs:11 and crates/brokkr-runtime/src/capabilities/tests.rs:7; (b) 7 lines at crates/brokkr-cli/src/doctor/capability_tests.rs:11 and crates/brokkr-runtime/tests/capability_launch.rs:38. The changed module declaration adjoining the existing write helper triggers these findings. The gate is authoritative, hence info severity. Resolve both within the allowed test scope without raising the clone baseline, rerun the gate, and update evidence/U9a1.md and task 45.8's verification evidence. The implementation record explains that its seat could not execute this gate; the review now supplies an observed failure. Exact coverage and supported-host CI remain explicitly pending as permitted. No defect in the settled specification or design was found.
